stories.title: Dodgers End 7-Game Losing Streak — Ohtani Walk-Off Hit in the 10th

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text:
The Dodgers' 7-game losing streak ended the same way most LA moments end.

Ohtani.

10th inning. Infield single deflects off the glove. Kyle Tucker scores from third. Dodgers 2, D-backs 1.

He can't pitch, but he can still win a game. 🔵 #Dodgers

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text:
Kyle Tucker homered in the 8th. Arizona tied it in the 9th on back-to-back triples. Then Ohtani singled off the fielder's glove in the 10th to end it.

Dodgers 2, D-backs 1. Seven-game losing streak over. Longest since 2017. #Dodgers #MLB

research.facts:
Dodgers End 7-Game Losing Streak
**Sources:** DodgersBeat, Sunday Guardian Live
**Key Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- **Date:** August 8, 2026
- **Result:** Dodgers 2, D-backs 1 (10 innings)
- **Venue:** Chase Field, Phoenix AZ
- **8th inning:** Kyle Tucker solo home run — Dodgers take 1-0 lead
- **9th inning:** Arizona tied it — Geraldo Perdomo and Corbin Carroll hit back-to-back triples
- **10th inning walk-off:** Shohei Ohtani lined infield single that deflected off Tim Tawa's glove; automatic runner Kyle Tucker (who had advanced to third on a wild pitch) scored the winning run
- **Losing streak:** 7 games — the Dodgers' longest since 2017
- **Ohtani pitching status:** Has not pitched since July 3 due to knee and biceps issues; no specific return-to-mound timeline given; stated he does not want to rush the process
- **Ohtani offense:** Continues to produce at the plate (confirmed hitting 2 HR during the losing streak period)
**MEDIUM confidence:**
- No Aug 9 Dodgers game result confirmed at time of research

stories.title: Red Sox 9-Game Win Streak Ends — 7-3 Loss to the Athletics

x_posts.label: Post 2-1
x_posts.text:
The Red Sox's 9-game win streak ended with a 7-3 loss to the Athletics on Friday.

Before it started, Boston was 32-46.

Before THAT, they ran a 15-game streak that tied the 1946 franchise record.

Same season. Same team. #RedSox #MLB

x_posts.label: Post 2-2
x_posts.text:
Had the Red Sox won one more game, they'd have been the first MLB team ever to post multiple 10-game winning streaks in a single season.

They got to 9.

Still historically remarkable. 32-46 before the turnaround. What a second half. #RedSox #MLB

research.facts:
Red Sox 9-Game Win Streak Ends
**Sources:** Boston.com, Washington Post, CBS Sports, Boston Globe
**Key Facts (HIGH confidence):**
- **Date:** August 8, 2026
- **Result:** Oakland Athletics 7, Red Sox 3
- **9-game streak:** Officially ended Aug 8
- **9th inning detail:** Boston left the bases loaded in a failed late comeback attempt
- **Earlier 15-game streak:** Red Sox had a separate 15-game winning streak (approximately July 8-23) — tied the 1946 franchise record (Ted Williams era); that streak ended before the 9-game run began
- **Team context:** Red Sox were 32-46 before the first 15-game streak; the dramatic mid-season turnaround is one of the AL's biggest stories
- **All-time context:** Had the 9-game streak extended to 10, they would have been the first team in MLB history to post multiple 10-plus-game winning streaks in a single season
**DISCREPANCY FLAG:**
- One CBS Boston headline references a loss to the Twins; two other sources (Boston.com, Washington Post) confirm 7-3 loss to the Athletics on Aug 8
- **Use the A's result** — supported by two independent sources with specific details
